title.narrative: Strengthening the health system in the North Achefer woreda, West Gojam Zone (Amhara Region) through Performance Based Financing

description.narrative: 1. 260,000 inhabitants in the West Gojam Zone 2. The West Gojam Health Department 3. Woreda Health Office and Finance and economic cooperation office 4. 8 primary health care units (PHCUs) and 1 District Hospitals (DH)

In 2015, Cordaid introduced PBF in the Ethiopian health sector, in the Borana zone (Oromia Region), while in 2019 a second PBF project started in the Jimma zone (also Oromia region). This expansion was made possible by the generous financial support of the Embassy of the Kingdom of The Netherlands (EKN) in Addis Ababa, which subsequently also took over the funding of the PBF intervention in Borana zone. From July 2021, the project covers 100% of the Health Facilities in Jimma and Borana. The current scope covers 11 hospitals, 165 health centres and 737 health posts, with a total population of 4,396,485. The expansion of project to North Achefer woreda of West Gojjam zone is essential in terms of the projects long term aim to institutionalise PBF within the Ethiopian health sector. To realise this aim it is necessary to demonstrate to the different levels of the Ethiopian Ministry of Health how PBF can contribute to an arid lands context (Borana) as well as in a highland context (Jimma and West Gojjam) to realising the Ministry’s objectives formulated in its HSTP-II.

The overarching objective of scaling up PBF in the North Achefer West Gojjam Zone is: “Improved availability and accessibility of good quality healthcare at primary and secondary level in the West Gojjam Zone (Amhara Region, Ethiopia), and a stronger health system at large, which supports the progressive realization of Universal Health Coverage (SDG 3.8) in this geographical area.”
The three (inter-related) targeted Outcomes are: 1. Improved Health Service Delivery in the North Achefer woreda of the West Gojjam Zone, reflected in: a. Increased utilization of good quality services b. Increased equity in access 2. Improved governance of health service delivery through: a. Increased capacity at the level of Woreda Health Offices and Zonal Health Department to perform their regulatory tasks and provide supportive supervision 3. Institutionalisation of PBF in the Ethiopian health system a. An enhanced health information system
